summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileosigmoid anastomosis, was admitted with a one-week history of worsening right-sided abdominal pain, increased watery bowel movements up to 100 per day, and bright red blood per rectum. He had recently started Tysabri therapy. CT imaging showed worsening wall thickening and hyperemia in the sigmoid colon, consistent with active inflammatory bowel disease, with no evidence of obstruction or infection. Stool studies and CMV testing were negative. He was initially treated with antibiotics, which were discontinued after negative cultures. Due to persistent symptoms, a steroid burst with prednisone was initiated in consultation with his specialist, leading to improvement in bowel frequency and pain. His back pain was evaluated with MRI, which showed stable degenerative disc disease without new neurological compromise; he was managed with Percocet and tizanidine. He improved clinically, was transitioned to oral medications, and discharged home on a prednisone taper, continued Tysabri and B12 injections, and pain regimen with follow-up planned with GI and spine services.
